title: SLO rapid-sprint + chaos experimentation playbook
content:
Summary:

This is a hands-on playbook for running a 6-week rapid-sprint program that combines SLO onramp work with targeted chaos experiments. The goal is to give feature teams a low-friction path to: (1) adopt a minimal SLO+alerting posture, (2) validate failures with lightweight chaos probes, and (3) iterate on safe fallback policies for model-serving routes.

Why this exists:
- We persistently see services with weak SLO definitions and poor failure-mode telemetry.
- Without validated failure experiments, rollouts and canaries miss correlated instability in downstream infra (KV cache / GPU node churn / routing fallbacks).
- A combined SLO + chaos approach accelerates confidence and surfaces thin places early in the release lifecycle.

Scope and non-goals:
- Scope: model-serving frontends, inference router, and two dependent subsystems (KV cache and batch dispatcher). Targeted teams: feature-owner + infra oncall + platform-engineering.
- Non-goals: full-scale chaos engineering program for infra (that lives under SRE). This playbook is a cross-functional sprint to produce reproducible, low-risk probes and SLO templates.

Program outcomes (measurable):
- Every participating route has a documented SLO (latency p99 and availability) and alert mapping in PagerDuty within 6 weeks.
- Two deterministic chaos probes executed against each route with roll-forward safety checks.
- Mean time to detect (MTTD) for injected failures reduced by 30% (compared to baseline week).
- One rollout policy updated to use a validated fallback model variant or region-based routing policy.

Stakeholders and roles:
- Feature Owner (FO): defines customer impact & acceptance criteria.
- Infra Oncall (IO): owns execution window and safe-stop authority during experiments.
- Platform Engineering (PE): provides templates (SLO, alerts), automation hooks, and observations.
- Observability SME: configures probes, traces, and dashboards.
- Product Ops: communicates to impacted customers for scheduled experiments.

High-level timeline (6-week sprint):
- Week 0 (prep): kickoff, route selection, risk assessment, baseline telemetry capture.
- Week 1: SLO drafting workshop & alert mapping; deploy minimal dashboards.
- Week 2: Runbook generation + failure-mode cataloging per route.
- Week 3: Chaos probe dry-run in staging with IO present.
- Week 4: Execution window #1 (production-lite) — low blast radius experiments and telemetry verification.
- Week 5: Execution window #2 — scaled probe matrix + rollback policy validation.
- Week 6: Consolidation, lessons learned, SLO sign-off, handoff to SRE for long-term adoption.

Checklist: prep (before Week 0)
- [ ] Identify 3 candidate routes (prefer mixed-traffic: low, medium, critical).
- [ ] Confirm IO availability and runbook owner.
- [ ] Baseline collection: p50/p95/p99 latency, 5xx rate, token consumption per request, caching hit-rate for 2 days.
- [ ] Create temporary dashboard using PE template: slo-rapid-<route>.
- [ ] Define blast-radius constraints for experiments (time window, percentage of traffic, region).

SLO template (minimal required fields):
- Service: <route-name>
- Objective: Availability = 99.5% (successful inference within 2s)
- Window: 30d rolling
- Indicators: 5xx count / successful requests, latency p99 measured at edge, function error rate if using tool-calls.
- Alert mapping: P0/P1 thresholds linked to PagerDuty escalation policy.
- Owner: Feature Owner + Platform Engineering contact.

Chaos probes (examples, low-risk first):
1) Latency amplification: inject 200ms synthetic delay into cache reads for 10% of requests for 5m. Validate latency SLO telemetry and routing fallback.
2) KV cache partial loss: throttle KV responses to 50% for a synthetic keyset to observe model serving fallback to cold-load.
3) Simulated model-variant failure: return malformed logits from a canary model instance for 1% of requests to validate validation layer and fallback variant routing.
4) Downstream bulkhead test: take down one batch dispatcher worker and route 10% traffic through degraded path; validate retry/backoff behavior.

Experiment safety and abort conditions:
- Abort immediately if production error rate exceeds 3x baseline for 15 consecutive minutes.
- Abort if p99 latency increases beyond SLA by >500ms for >10 minutes.
- IO has live authority to stop experiments. Any abort triggers postmortem within 48 hours.

Instrumentation and telemetry checklist:
- Trace sampling enabled for probe traffic with tag slo-rapid=<run-id>.
- Alert rules created in a quiet channel: slo-rapid-alerts@ops (suppression during windows except for abort thresholds).
- Dashboards: p50/p95/p99 lines, error-rate histograms, fallback-rate meter, model-variant switch counts.
- Synthetic request generator: PE provides a small client that signs requests and marks them as probe traffic.

Runbooks and playbooks (deliverables):
- Route-specific runbook: intent, SLO, probes allowed, abort thresholds, rollback steps, ownership.
- Quick-stop play: how to remove injected traffic (feature flag, scaling down canary, kill probe job).
- Postmortem template: impact summary, timeline, telemetry excerpts, corrective actions.

Communication plan:
- Pre-exec (48h): message to #sre-ops and impacted product channels, update status page Private/Dev preview if customer impacted.
- During-exec: dedicated Zoom bridge + Slack thread with IO and PE leads.
- Post-exec: 24–48h debrief doc posted to the route folder and a short summary to the reliability-broadcaster mailing list.

Success criteria for route sign-off:
- SLO defined, alerts mapped, and runbook created.
- At least two chaos probes executed and observed without violating abort conditions.
- One control-plane change validated (e.g., fallback variant works, region fallback triggers).
- Observability SME confirms adequate telemetry coverage for long-term monitoring.

Bootstrap templates and utilities (links):
- SLO draft template (use and copy): CONFL-OPS-4021
- Probe client: https://github.com/redwood-inference/observability/tree/main/probe-client
- Dashboard template: /dashboards/template/slo-rapid-basic (PE will import)

Risks and mitigations:
- Risk: experiments inadvertently touch high-value customers. Mitigation: use feature flags and explicit allowlist of test accounts; coordinate with Product Ops.
- Risk: noisy alerts during execution. Mitigation: route alerts to slo-rapid-alerts and use suppression for known signals; keep abort thresholds strict.
- Risk: insufficient observability on a route. Mitigation: delay experiments until minimum telemetry is in place (baseline step mandatory).

Decision log (sample entries):
- 2026-05-13: Selected 3 routes — inference-edge-v2, reranker-canary, batch-merge.
- 2026-05-20: Agreed minimal availability objective 99.5% (30d) for non-critical routes, higher for core billing-dependent routes.

Next steps (action items):
- PE: publish probe-client container with tagging and credentials (due 2026-05-18).
- FO: prepare user-impact acceptance criteria and allowlist (due 2026-05-19).
- Observability SME: import dashboard template and capture 48h baseline (due 2026-05-20).
- IO: schedule two execution windows (dates suggested in calendar invite).

Appendix: quick templates (copy-paste)
- Minimal SLO: "Availability: 99.5% within 30d rolling window; Indicator: requests with latency <2s and no 5xx"
- Probe job CLI (example): "probe-client run --route inference-edge-v2 --mode delay --pct 10 --delay-ms 200 --duration 300"

Notes to reviewers: This doc is intentionally pragmatic — it trades exhaustive coverage for a reproducible, low-friction play that teams can repeat. Feedback wanted on the abort thresholds and the trial calendar cadence.
